title: GPU Chargeback Exporter and IaC Pattern Playbook
author: Miles Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook describes a pragmatic, reproducible pattern for exporting GPU usage metrics at tenant granularity, coupling those metrics into a chargeback pipeline, and managing the Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD tests, dashboards, and runbooks needed to operate the system safely. It focuses on a sidecar-based exporter + node/agent instrumentation approach that works across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Goals

- Produce high-cardinality, cost-attributable metrics (gpu_seconds, gpu_memory_bytes, cuda_kernel_time_ms) labeled by tenant_id, model_id, and runtime_variant.
- Ensure metrics are cheap to scrape and easy to aggregate for daily/weekly chargeback and real-time quota enforcement.
- Provide a Terraform module pattern for deployment to multiple accounts/regions with consistent scraping rules and RBAC.
- Integrate into CI/CD so that changes to scraping, metric names, or label schema are validated before promotion.
- Include a clear oncall runbook for reconciling billing mismatches.

Scope and non-goals

- Scope: tenant-level GPU runtime usage (inference and eval clusters) across Redwood-managed runtime pools.
- Non-goal: replacing per-VM cloud billing exports; this playbook augments those with application-level signal for internal chargeback and cost-smoothing algorithms.

Architecture summary

1) Sidecar exporter (go or rust) runs alongside GPU runtime process and exposes Prometheus metrics on /metrics with labels: tenant_id, job, model, variant, quantization_profile.
2) Node-level agent exports node-level attributes (gpu_type, driver_version, instance_id) and attaches to metrics as stable labels for downstream reconciliation.
3) Central metrics ingestion (Prometheus remote_write -> Cortex/Thanos) with short retention for high-cardinality joins plus hourly rollup jobs that emit aggregated per-tenant daily totals into billing storage (BigQuery/Snowflake).
4) Terraform module deploys sidecar as a DaemonSet (k8s) or systemd unit (onprem) and configures ServiceMonitors/scrape targets and IAM roles for read-only access to kube/node metadata.

Label contract (required)

- tenant_id: internal tenant GUID (redwood-tenant-xxxx)
- job: runtime cluster name (inference, eval, sandbox)
- model_id: model identifier (gpt-7b/quantized-v2)
- variant: cpu|gpu|gpu-preemptible
- gpu_type: A100|H100|T4

Note: label names are stable strings. Any change must follow the "metric-schema" CI gate below.

Terraform / IaC pattern

This repository pattern has three modules:

- modules/gpu-chargeback-exporter - deploys exporter (DaemonSet/systemd), ServiceMonitor, configmap for exporter flags
- modules/metrics-gateway - configures Cortex/Thanos remote_write endpoints and credentials
- tenants/tenant-bootstrap - per-tenant wrapper that wires tenant metadata secrets and grants read-only tagging permissions

Recommended module interface (table)

| input | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| cluster_name | string | Cluster identifier used for job label |
| exporter_image | string | Docker image for the exporter |
| scrape_port | number | Port exposed by exporter |
| tenant_selector | map(string) | Labels/selectors identifying pods to instrument |
| extra_labels | map(string) | Freeform labels to attach to metrics |

Example Terraform snippet (usage):

```hcl
module "gpu_chargeback" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood.ai/infra/modules//gpu-chargeback-exporter?ref=v1.2.0"

  cluster_name    = var.cluster_name
  exporter_image  = "ghcr.io/redwood/gpu-chargeback-exporter:v1.2.0"
  scrape_port     = 9191
  tenant_selector = { "app.kubernetes.io/role" = "inference-pod" }
}
```

Prometheus scrape / exporter config example

Prometheus ServiceMonitor snippet (k8s):

```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: gpu-chargeback-exporter
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gpu-chargeback-exporter
  endpoints:
  - port: metrics
    interval: 30s
    honorLabels: true
    metricRelabelings:
    - sourceLabels: ["tenant_id"]
      regex: ".+"
      action: keep
```

Exporter design notes (implementation-level)

- Host metrics collection inside the exporter using a shared memory interface or metrics API provided by the runtime when possible to avoid expensive process sampling.
- Maintain a local ring buffer of per-tenant GPU time slices to guard against transient spikes; flush to Prometheus as counters with monotonic semantics.
- Provide a metrics-compatibility endpoint (/schema) which returns the current label and metric names — CI gate uses this for schema validation.

CI/CD validations and tests

Every change that touches exporter image, metrics names, or Terraform modules must run the following pipeline tests (Buildkite/GitHub Actions):

1) Unit tests for exporter code (coverage threshold >= 75%).
2) Metrics schema linter: run exporter in container and call /schema, compare against approved-schema.json. If new metric or label added, require a metrics-compatibility-ADR and reviewer signoff.
3) Terraform plan validation: run `terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=ci.tfvars` against a dry-run environment. Failing plans block promotion.
4) End-to-end smoke: deploy exporter to sandbox cluster, generate synthetic tenant load with `scripts/load-gen --tenant synthetic-tenant-1 --gpu-seconds 60`, assert that aggregated daily rollup job writes expected row to BigQuery (within 3% tolerance).

Buildkite example stage (snippet):

```yaml
steps:
  - label: "Validate metrics schema"
    command: |
      docker run --rm ghcr.io/redwood/gpu-chargeback-exporter:pr-$BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST /bin/exporter --print-schema > schema.json
      python tools/metrics_linter.py schema.json approved-schema.json
```

Rollout and upgrade strategy

- Canary: deploy exporter image to 5% of nodes (nodeSelector: canary=true) and run smoke-generator for canary tenants. Monitor metric cardinality and remote_write ingestion rate for 24h.
- Gradual: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours assuming no metric explosion or ingestion errors.
- Fallback: if remote_write errors exceed 0.1% of samples or cardinality grows > 3x baseline, pause rollout and rollback image tag.

Cost and cardinality controls

- Metrics sampling interval default: 30s. For high-traffic clusters allow coarse 60s sampling for cost-reduction.
- Downsampling rule: use a daily rollup job that aggregates per-tenant GPU seconds; raw high-cardinality metrics kept for 72h only.
- Cardinality guardrails in exporter to drop non-critical labels under load (configurable via configmap).

Operational runbook (for oncall and chargeback disputes)

1) Alert: billing-discrepancy-high triggers when exported tenant GPU cost deviates > 8% from cloud-provider charge for the same account/day.
2) Initial triage (5–15m):
   - Identify tenant_id and date range from alert.
   - Query raw Prometheus metrics: `promql: sum by (tenant_id) (increase(gpu_seconds[24h]))`
   - Pull cloud billing export for same time window and filter by instance tags.
3) Common causes and remediation:
   - Missing node labels -> attach node metadata (follow node-labeling checklist).
   - Remote_write ingestion gap -> check Cortex/Thanos ingesters for tombstones and OOM events; escalate to observability oncall.
   - Duplicate label values caused by multiple exporters attached to same pod -> deploy exporter with `hostNetwork: false` and dedupe logic.
4) Reconciliation and correction (post-incident):
   - Recompute daily rollup and write correction row to billing warehouse with a `correction_reason` tag.

Example queries (Prometheus / BigQuery)

- Prometheus (hourly tenant usage):
  `sum by (tenant_id) (increase(gpu_seconds[1h]))`

- BigQuery (daily rollup table):
  ```sql
  SELECT tenant_id, DATE(ts) AS day, SUM(gpu_seconds) AS gpu_seconds
  FROM `redwood_billing.gpu_daily_rollup`
  WHERE day BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 14 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  GROUP BY tenant_id, day
  ```

Dashboards and alerts (recommended)

- Chargeback overview dashboard: table of tenant daily GPU seconds, rolling 7d delta, percent of total; owner: infra-finops.
- Exporter health: scrape errors, last_scrape_duration_seconds, exporter_restarts_total (threshold > 3/hr)
- Cardinality watch: unique label combinations vs baseline (alert > 2x)

Ownership and SLAs

- Primary owner: infra-observability team (pager: infra-obs@redwood.ai)
- Secondary: gpu-fleet team for driver/hardware issues
- SLO: exporter availability 99.5% (measured as successful scrapes per target per 24h)
- Cost SLO: rollup and billing export to Warehouse within 4 hours of day boundary (monitored job latency).

Privacy and security considerations

- tenant_id is internal; ensure exporters never emit PII. Use hashed tenant identifiers when exporting to 3rd-party systems.
- Grant the exporter read-only IAM roles scoped to node metadata; avoid broad permissions.

Testing checklist for change PRs

- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] Metrics schema linter passed and reviewer tagged
- [ ] Terraform plan validated in CI
- [ ] E2E sandbox smoke passed
- [ ] Release notes include any metrics/label changes and migration plan

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands

- Check exporter logs (k8s): `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=gpu-chargeback-exporter --tail 500`
- Check Prometheus target: `kubectl -n monitoring get servicemonitor gpu-chargeback-exporter -o yaml`
- Re-run daily rollup locally: `python tools/run_rollup.py --date 2025-02-19 --output debug.csv`
